en: The Sun is so large that about 1.3 million Earths could fit inside it.
The Moon is approximately 384,400 kilometers away from Earth, which is about 30 Earth diameters.
On the Mohs hardness scale, diamond is the hardest mineral at ten, while talc is the softest at one.
The hottest air temperature ever recorded on Earth was 56.7 degrees Celsius in Death Valley, California, in 1913.
Oceans hold about 97 percent of all Earth's water, leaving only 3 percent as fresh water.
A magnitude eight earthquake releases about 32 times more energy than a magnitude seven earthquake.
Proxima Centauri is the closest star to our solar system, located about 4.24 light-years away from Earth.
Clay soil particles are the smallest at less than 0.002 millimeters, while sand particles are the largest at up to 2 millimeters.
Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system, with a mass more than 300 times that of Earth.
An average cumulus cloud contains about 500,000 kilograms of water droplets, weighing roughly as much as 100 elephants.
The 1883 eruption of Krakatoa produced a sound so loud it was heard 3,000 miles away.
Earth is approximately 4.54 billion years old, which is about one-third the age of the entire universe.
